How much light each face of the tree collects in a day (DLI, mol/m²/day) — measured daylight baseline plus the placed fixtures. Bands from the tree-care fact base: light that falls short thins a face; only a face held near zero long-term goes bare.

Night: these bands score Part A's daytime grow lighting (08:00–18:00) — unaffected by the decorative uplights currently shown.

ESTIMATE — beam-angle + catalogue lumens; real photometry (IES) pending; empirical target set by the PAR-meter mock-up. = display-face pad (its foyer-facing side counts toward the headline).

Pads, trunk and the Scan cloud are MEASURED (nursery 3D scan 2026-09-04: photogrammetry + LiDAR, pot-scaled, trunk-base frame). Fixture and viewpoint positions remain design values; anchor capacities are gated on the site surveyper-fixture-type dispersion models (round point cone / rectangular flood, wider than tall / the sill strip as a 2 m line source / horticultural panel spread); IES will replace. Flux from beam angle + catalogue lumens (PPF ≈ lumens ÷ 68, the 3000 K rule, applied to 2700 K as a labelled approximation). Daylight baseline is the measured-model daily figure per height band and face; glass bounce onto the foyer face (plausibly +1–3 DLI) is excluded — conservative. The Day/Night switch changes the visual only, not the daily light arithmetic. The tree-position controls are what-ifs (spec §3a): the slide moves the whole tree assembly toward the courtyard (daylight floors held constant — orientation/height-based, treated as unchanged by a few cm of slide; approximation); the flip rotates the whole assembly 180° about the trunk axis — display-face detection, aspect relevance and the orientation-based daylight floors follow the rotated geometry. Fixture aims follow the tree in both. Spec default is the 11 cm courtyard slide (owner-ruled 2026-08-12; the pole heads are re-optimised for it — every pad clears the die band), current (un-flipped) orientation; drag the slide to 0 to see the earlier centred layout.
